text: The model looked at three key pieces of the applicant’s credit history. First, the borrower has one account that was 30‑59 days past due; this adds about 0.50 points to the default‑risk side, nudging the score upward. Second, the applicant’s revolving‑credit utilization is low—about 10 % of the available limit—which pulls the risk down by roughly 0.44 points, a strong mitigating factor. Third, the person holds a relatively high number of open credit lines and loans (19), which contributes another 0.43 points to the risk side. When the model combines these influences, the low utilization outweighs the two risk‑increasing signals, leading it to label the overall profile as low risk despite the listed probability.
